update.title: M09 humility: existing humility claims reconciled in the touched chapters
update.researcher_instruction: "We agreed that the claim reconciliation will take place when a particular chapter is touched with updates.  I cannot see how you can update the chapter in the narrative with new information without reviewing the current claims, and ensuring that the claims in the narrative are recorded in the register." and "The method I am proposing is to reconcile the existing claims for the concepts that is being updated, for instance in this case humility and related.  to reconcile every claim in the chapter will cause severe disruption because it is not the focus and cannot be resolved in this session." (2026-10-15)
update.method: In the 15 chapters touched by update 141, the existing passages on humility and related concepts (63 by word search, plus the edited passages that keep older text) were read against the register. Matched to the claims of update 141 or to the untold legacy claims 1-4, 2-2 and 5-2 by new tellings; 8 statements with no claim registered (n1-n3, p1-p5); C-188 restated (its count of four passages was incomplete across the narrative); two statements beyond their verses restated in the text (10.7 "not wrong in itself"; Ch 14 "God's reason is tender"). Passages that only quote, or that belong to other concepts (fear, authority, flesh, the gentle waters of Isa 8:6, the gentle lamb of Jer 11:19), were left for their own strands.
update.claims_changed_note: 8 new claims (n1-n3, p1-p5); C-188 restated; 40 tellings on existing passages; legacy 1-4, 2-2, 5-2 now told
update.not_woven_note: Other concepts in the touched chapters (soul, the Spirit given, heart as centre, fear, authority) are not reconciled here; they wait for their strands (researcher ruling on scope).
update.quote_note: no new quotations; two restatements remove words

new.text: God's anger is roused to save the humble, and the earth falls still before it

new.text: The parts of the inner person give way in sequence: soul, spirit, heart under an enemy, then a turn; heart, then spirit, then body under sorrow
new.beyond_text: reads Psa 143:3-6 and Pro 15:13 with 17:22 as one chain each

new.text: The offering is weighed by what is inside the one who brings it: an ear opened, the law in the heart, a broken heart, a love that lasts

new.text: Pride is placed in the heart and in the spirit

new.text: In pride, thinking goes wrong at the point of comparing: a person makes himself like God, or shrinks God to his own size
new.beyond_text: sets the self-exaltation of Isa 14 and Eze 28 beside Psa 50:21

new.text: Pride can grow from a beauty that was given: given, blameless, then trade, violence and a proud heart

new.text: Pride can design its own honour, and the honour it designed becomes the measure of its fall

edit.text: What God looks to is set against a religious act in the humility passages (the fast, the walk, the house, the broken heart), as in the other passages gathered in 13.1; the offering follows the broken heart
edit.note: The first wording ("In four passages") counted only the humility passages; 13.1 Delight gathers more (Isa 1:11-13; Psa 40:6-8; Hos 6:6; Mat 9:13; 12:7). Found in the reconciliation of #2152.
